full_judgment:
2. Facts. briefly stated are that the respondents as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.211 of 2009 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka against the defendant for partition of the suit property claiming saham therein as per their shares. In the suit the plaintiffs filed an application under Order XL Rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) for appointment of receiver in respect of the suit property stating, inter-alia, that their father Captain Shamsul Huda took active part in the liberation war from Comilla Cantonment and was killed during the war. He left behind a widow named Hasina Banu and the plaintiffs, a son and a daughter. The plaintiffs being the children of a martyr and their mother having not taken a second husband, the Military Lands and Cantonments Directorate, Military of Defence, Dhaka Cantonment on 09.06.1982 allotted the suit land in favour of their mother vide letter No.6/MIC/ME0/286; the lease deed in respect of the allotted land was executed on 22.09.1982. After getting possession of allotted land, the deceased mother of the plaintiffs constructed building thereon on obtaining permission from the proper authority and started living there with them. Subsequently, the plaintiffs' had left for London for higher study, but their mother lived there. Plaintiffs' mother married their paternal uncle Mirja Shamsul Wazed, the defendant in 1988 and she died on 4th December, 1989 in a mysterious road accident at Saedabad under police station Serajgonj. On receipt of the news of death of the plaintiffs' mother plaintiff  No. 1 came to Bangladesh and performed the job of her burial. After the death of Hasina Banu, the defendant as her husband inherited 1⁄4 share in the suit property whereas the plaintiffs being her son and daughter inherited 2/4and 1⁄4 share respectively, that is 3⁄4 share jointly. While in ejmali possession of the suit property, the plaintiff left for London to continue his study there giving the defendant the responsibility to look after the suit property and also to realize rents from the tenants. The defendant did not pay the plaintiffs' due share of the rents received from the tenants of the building situated in the suit land and told them that bulk portion of the rents was spent in paying various bills and in maintaining the building and only a partly amount of money has remained as 

 balance, but that amount was not also paid to the plaintiffs on various pleas. The plaintiffs having understood about the ill motive of the defendant asked him to give them their share in the building in the suit land but he killed time on this or that plea. The defendant did not give any account about rents realized from the tenants. The defendant has been realizing rents from the tenant but is not giving any thing to the plaintiffs and thus, he is being personally benefited for which the plaintiffs are being subjected to irreparable financial loss for the proper maintenance of the building and hence prayed for appointment of receiver for proper maintenance of the building in the suit property and to realize rents from the tenants. 

 3. The application was opposed by the defendant by filing written objection contending, inter-alia, that mother of the plaintiffs being a housewife had no money and in her income tax file, she clearly stated that in 1997 she spent Tk.36.084.00 from her personal savings and so he started the construction of the building with his own money. Subsequently, the plaintiff's mother took loan of Tk.6(six) lakh from hank and the defendant took loan of Tk.10(ten) lakh from his subordinate soldiers and with that money a 2(two) storied building and a bed room over 1st  floor were constructed. In 2001, the defendant got a revised plan passed for construction of a 6(six) storied building and constructed upto 4th floor on the existing first floor by the money which he collected by selling his pension, borrowing Tk.25,00,000.00 from his business and by taking Tk.25,00,000.00 each from Major Md. Kamran, Major Aminul Islam and Hajee Shafiqur Rahman towards earnest money against the sale of the apartment. Plaintiff No.2 Habiba Shamas married one Moksudul Islam, son of Syed Rahman without any permission from her mother as well as the defendant and after five years the said marriage was accepted on certain terms. As per the said terms Muksedul Alam went to London. The defendant also sent plaintiff No.2 to London by spending about Tk.5,00,000.00 (five) lakh. Thereafter, in 1997 the defendant sent plaintiff No.1 to London for higher education by spending Tk.6,00,000.00 and upto 2004 he spent about Tk.20,00,000.00 towards his education expenses through various persons. The marriage of plaintiff No.2 was dissolved in London and at one stage she was found missing. The defendant went to London to look for plaintiff No.2 and spent Tk.30,00,000.00 for the purpose, but he could not meet her. Though the plaintiffs are the owners of the suit land to the extent of 3⁄4 share, they cannot have any claim on the building constructed thereon; it is the defendant who constructed the building by his own money and, therefore, the plaintiffs had no cause of action to file the suit as well as the application for appointment of receiver. Every month a sum of Tk.85,635 is being spent towards the payment of debt which is more than the rents realized from the tenants of the building. The debt would be liquidated in 2015. However, the defendant admitted that he would get 1⁄4 share in the suit land as husband of Hasina Banu and the plaintiffs would get the rest. 

 6. Mr. M.A. Samad, learned Counsel, entering caveat on behalf of the respondents, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order by submitting that in the facts and circumstances of the case particularly the fact that the defendant has denied the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs in the building in the suit land, the if the rents are not High Court Division rightly affirmed the order passed by the learned Joint District Judge appointing receiver and as such, no interference is called for by this Court. 

 7. From the order of the learned Joint District Judge, it appears that he allowed the prayer for appointment of receiver in respect of the suit property with the finding, inter-alia, that although the defendant admitted that the plaintiffs are the owner of the suit land to the extent of -3/4share, he denied their right, title and interest in the building constructed thereon. The learned Joint District Judge further found that admittedly the plaintiffs live in London and the defendant by denying their right and title in the building already accepted Tk.50.00,000.00 each from Major Md. Kamran and Major Md. Aminul Islam as advance for selling the apartment constructed on the suit land though the suit property was not partitioned. The learned Joint District Judge concluded by saying that from the conduct of the defendant such as taking of money in advance against the sale of the apartment, taking of advance rent and his denial of the plaintiffs' right and title in the constructed building prima facie proved that if receiver was not appointed in respect of the suit property, there was chance of destroying the suit .property by the defendant in the absence of the plaintiffs who are living in London. The learned Joint District Judge further observed that in the circumstances in case, the plaintiffs get decree in the suit, there shall be legal complicacy in getting the fruit of the decree. The learned Joint District Judge further concluded that the plaintiffs are the owners of the suit property to the extent of 3/4 share 

 8. The High Court Division while confirming the order of appointment of receiver noted the facts that although the property was not partitioned, the defendant without taking any consent of the plaintiffs received Tk.12,00,000.00 from 3(three) persons namely, Major Kamran, Major Aminul Islam and Shafiqur Rahman with the assurance that they would be "provided with (sold) one flat upon constructing building upon the 21⁄2 storied building already constructed by plaintiffs' mother". The High Court Division in line with the learned Joint District Judge found that although the plaintiffs are the owners of the suit land to the extent of the 3/4share, the defendant being their step father denied their ownership in the building. The High Court DivisiOn has further noted that the defendant has been occupying the entire building and realizing rents from the tenants but has not provided any paper showing actual receipt of rents from the tenants to prove his sincerity and bonafide; there was nothing on record to show what amount was spent towards loan and what amount was paid towards taxes. The High Court Division found that from the written objection it was very much clear that the defendant with an evil motive has taken active attempt to sell out the apartment already constructed upon the 21⁄2storied building and very cleverly denied the ownership of the plaintiffs therein saying that they have no interest or claim in the building upon the suit land. The High Court Division noticed that 21⁄2  storied building on the suit land was completed in 1989 by Hasina Banu, mother of the plaintiffs and the total cost incurred for the construction was Tk.17,42,241.00 by taking loan from HBFC as well as Rupali Bank Limited. The High Court Division further found that the materials on record do not show that the defendant took any permission from the plaintiffs in entering into any contract with other persons for selling out any floor or any apartment. The High Court Division also noted that the defendant did not take any permission from the plaintiffs for undertaking construction upon 21⁄2 storied building already constructed by their mother; there is nothing on record that any farthing was given to the plaintiffs after the demise of their mother and no account was shown to them with regard to the income of the building and by now the defendant has taken second wife and the "the plaintiffs have become step son and daughter". The High Court Division concluded by observing that the management and occupation of the building in the hands of the defendant is not safe and as such, it is a clear case of appointment of receiver. 

 11. From the facts as revealed in the plaint, the application for appointment of receiver and the written objection filed thereto, it is an admitted position that the land on which the building has been constructed was allotted to Hasina Banu, mother of the plaintiffs as the widow of martyr husband Captain Shamsul Huda who sacrificed his life in the liberation war. Subsequently, Hasina Banu married the defendant, the paternal uncle of the plaintiffs and according to the Muslim Law of Inheritance, the defendant inherited only 1⁄4 share in the suit property and the plaintiffs jointly inherited  3/4 share therein. It is also an admitted fact that during the life time of Hasina Banu, construction of 21⁄2  storied building on the suit land was completed. The plaintiffs' case is that before they left for London, they left the Suit property under the care and management of the defendant including realization of rents from the tenants, but he did not give them their due share of rents which he realized from the tenants of the building on the suit land. On the demand of their shares, the defendant told that hulk of the account of the rents realized from The tenants was spent in paying various bills and maintaining the building and after that only a partly amount remained in balance and that was also not being paid to them. As against this, the defendant in his written objection has categorically stated that though the plaintiffs are the owners of the land on which the building is situated to the extent of 3/4  share, they have no right and title on the building constructed thereon. The defendant has also asserted that it is he who constructed 21⁄2 storied building on the suit land as their mother being a house wife had no money to construct the building. More dangerous thing is that the defendant himself has asserted that he obtained a revised plan in 2001 to construct a 6(six) storied building on the existing building and completed construction upto 41/2 floor by his own money as well as by taking Tk.1,20,00,000.00 from 3(three) persons, namely Major Md. Kamran, Major Aminul Islam and Hajee Shafiqur Rahman towards earnest money against the sale of apartment in the building. Admittedly, the defendant did not take any consent from the plaintiffs, the owners of the suit land to the extent of 3/4 share to undertake construction work on the existing building and also in taking advance from the above mentioned persons against the sale of the apartment to them. The plaintiffs have also alleged that the defendant is not giving them their due share of the rents realized from the tenants. The defendant, in support of his case that bulk portion of the realized rents from the tenants were spent in paying various bills and in maintaining the property, has failed to file any document and paper. The defendant has also failed to show that a single farthing was paid to the plaintiffs after the death of their mother out of the rents realized from the tenants in the building. 

 12. From the above, it prima facie appears to us that the defendant is treating the suit property as the absolute owner in clear denial of the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs therein and in the circumstances, the element of apprehension of alienation and wasting of the suit property is very much there, so the plaintiffs have made out a special case and appointment of receiver. In the facts and circumstances of the case the learned Joint District Judge rightly allowed the application for appointment of receiver filed by the plaintiffs in respect of the suit property in the terms as mentioned in his order and the High Court Division rightly affirmed the same.
